acceptance_arm.why_value_gate_off: its default flipped ON in #10996; an arm that declares itself OFF must pin the explicit 0 or it measures the predicate's population
acceptance_arm.read_back: The set is CLOSED over the modules named in tests/test_7949_c2_door.py::path_modules — a pointer, not a count, because a count in this field went stale three rounds running — and what `tests/test_7949_c2_door.py` enforces mechanically is the CENSUS over that list, not the list's membership: `path_modules` is a hand-maintained tuple, and every ``TORTOISE_*`` read inside those modules must be classified (arm seam, pin, declared input, or an acknowledged non-seam with a stated reason) or the suite reds. Membership is hand-kept, so a read added to a module OUTSIDE that tuple is not caught by it; the same chain's infrastructure reads (record DSN, packs dir, embedding gates, store connection) are inputs, deliberately outside the partition, the sdk/hosted_api helpers those two hops call are in neither, which is the measured gap tracked as #11410, and a new derived module is a one-line change to the test's path_modules. Every value is re-read from os.environ after setting and a mismatch REFUSES the run.. Cycle 7 added the two reads the closure was still missing, both consulted on the acceptance path and previously in no pin, no ledger row and no closure: TORTOISE_CONTEXT_ENRICH (context_enrich.enrich_enabled, reached as sdk.capture_session(enrich_fn=_capture_enriched_texts) — it rewrites the text each turn embeds) pinned off (fail-safe OFF, so the pin matches today's behaviour), and TORTOISE_JSON_MODE (model_adapters, default-ON and read per call, flips the request's response_format) pinned to "1". A new read inserted in enrich_enabled() left the closure pin GREEN at the previous head (measured). Cycle 8 added TORTOISE_CHANGE_FEED (change_feed.py, reached via sdk._change_feed_enabled on PointRevised) pinned off: an ambient =1 adds a :GraphEvent to the graph the run writes and the probe's S6 step witness prints that count (measured on one capture of the registered corpus: 2 vs 3 :GraphEvent). Cycle 9 added TORTOISE_IDENTIFIER_TOKENS (sparse.py:226, default-ON, read through projection/entities.py:1480 point_identifier_aliases on the write path), pinned to its shipped default 1: it rewrites search_keys on every :Point the run writes, and the registered corpus yields no aliases either way (measured: 0 of 27 points, 0 of 7 fixtures), so the pin makes the population shell-insensitive without moving a number. tortoise/sparse.py is now in path_modules.. Cycle 10 added TORTOISE_SUBJECT_TAU_HI/_LO (subject_binding.py:189 via bind_point_subjects, read through a PARAMETER so no resolver sees them) pinned unset, and made the closure read LITERALS as well as resolved reads: measured 0.90 -> bound at the defaults, suspected with TORTOISE_SUBJECT_TAU_HI=0.99, i.e. the :aboutSubject/:aboutObject edge is not written. Cycle 11 added TORTOISE_STATE_VALUE_VERBATIM (extractor_v2._state_value_verbatim_enforced, the one name #11449 gave the #10360 carve-out's write-path off-switch; read PER EMITTED POINT at extractor_v2.py:11361 and handed to the rule as armed=), pinned to its shipped default 1: the switch is default-ON, and with it off the emit site takes no judgment at all — no refusal, no hard-cut disclosure, and refused_value_contents/refused_value_slots stay empty so the resurrection guard cannot fire either — so an ambient =0 WRITES a rewritten value that main withholds and the point population grows under a door whose header would still claim the pin held. It arrived AFTER cycle 10's closure (landed in #11449, 2026-11-07) and the census redded on it for every PR until it was classified, which is the closure doing its job. The pin is the shipped default, so it moves no number and makes the population shell-insensitive. This branch (`#11534`) adds `TORTOISE_PARTIAL_GAP_FILL` (`extractor_v2._partial_gap_fill_enabled`, its one `env_flag` read, consumed by the S2.2b-ADD gap-fill stage BEFORE S3) pinned OFF: an armed `=1` spends a bounded model call ADDING items to the embed list, i.e. it changes the population of the capture this door scores, under a header that would still claim the door held. It is DEFAULT OFF, and unset is the only state the registered corpus was scored under, so the pin matches today's behaviour and needs no value. The #11534 entry is `TORTOISE_PARTIAL_GAP_FILL` at `probes/capstone_measure.py:498`. The Cycle-11 entry this cite-shift argument is about is `TORTOISE_STATE_VALUE_VERBATIM` at `probes/capstone_measure.py:527`. It is NOT cite-neutral, and the branch that authored it said it was kept on ONE source line for that reason: the union squashed as a1dff7cec8 landed it with a 10-line comment above it instead, and that 11-line insert moved every downstream cite in the file by +11 (measured: "arm": arm_record( 4008 at a1dff7cec8^ -> 4019 at a1dff7cec8). Nothing in DOOR_PINNED_ON is exempt, but the scope is DOWNSTREAM: a line inserted inside the tuple moves every probes/capstone_measure.py:NNNN cite BELOW it, and no cite above it. The bundle demonstrates both halves — it carries :275-283, which sits above the tuple and did NOT move when a1dff7cec8's :278 hunk changed no line COUNT, and it carries :2747-2749, which sits below: a1dff7cec8 moved that window :2713-2715 -> :2724-2726 (+11, the same shift as everything below the tuple), #11517's own `TORTOISE_RENARRATE_KEEP_RATE` arm inside `DOOR_PINNED_OFF` (`7dabb59e0f45`) moved it :2724-2726 -> :2736-2738 (+12), `#11523`'s rewrap of `DOOR_PINNED_ON`'s own comment (`8212c41eff`) moved it :2736-2738 -> :2738-2740 (+2), and `#11534`'s own `TORTOISE_PARTIAL_GAP_FILL` arm inside `DOOR_PINNED_OFF` then moved it once more :2738-2740 -> :2747-2749 (+9) - so the window's final position is not any single commit's, it is the sum of the four.
